text:
ConocoPhillips fell 2.6% today as crude oil prices dropped sharply on growing hopes for U.S.-Iran peace talks. Diplomatic efforts by Qatari mediators and statements from Trump administration officials suggesting a desire for peaceful resolution spooked the oil market—crude fell to session lows Monday morning. When oil prices weaken, integrated oil companies like ConocoPhillips face lower revenues from production, which explains the stock's immediate decline.

The dip reverses some of the stock's strong two-week run (up 3.3%), which had coincided with oil climbing toward $154/barrel on Friday. The gap between U.S. crude ($103/barrel today) and world crude ($123/barrel) underscores persistent supply concerns despite the diplomatic thaw—if tensions ease further, that premium could compress even more, weighing on margins for companies producing in the region.
